claims.text: As-deposited FeMnNiGeSi-type thin films or nanoribbons have constrained heat-transfer dynamics.
These nanoscale FeMnNiGeSi-type samples exhibit pronounced hysteresis because of nanoscale interfacial effects.
A few-nanometer Cu or Ag interlayer at the film-substrate interface will increase interfacial thermal conduction.
Patterning nanoribbons to increase substrate contact area will improve interfacial heat transfer.
Surface and interfacial phenomena dominate the response at the specified nanoscale dimensions.
Enhanced interfacial thermal conduction will produce a more uniform temperature distribution during rapid magnetization and demagnetization cycles.
Enhanced interfacial thermal conduction will mitigate localized hot spots during cycling.
Local thermal gradients can disturb equilibrium magnetization processes.
Reducing local thermal gradients will stabilize magnetization processes.
Stabilizing magnetization processes through improved heat dissipation will reduce hysteretic energy loss.
Improved interfacial heat dissipation will strengthen the magnetocaloric response.
Thermally modified samples will exhibit narrower magnetic hysteresis loops than the as-deposited baseline.
Thermally modified samples will exhibit a larger magnetocaloric temperature change than the as-deposited baseline.
Unmodified samples are expected to have larger hysteresis loops because of limited interfacial heat transfer.
Temperature non-uniformity caused by limited interfacial heat transfer dampens the magnetocaloric effect in unmodified samples.
The proposed effects apply under low fields of approximately tens to a few hundred Oe near room temperature when interfacial heat-transfer limitations are significant.
The response may differ in bulk samples or under high applied fields.
The magnitude of hysteresis reduction and temperature-change enhancement depends on interlayer thickness, deposition uniformity, and nanoscale heat-transfer dynamics.
